Reprints are the hard part of scanning Magic cards

Magic: The Gathering has a reprint problem that Pokemon does not have to the same degree. A staple card can exist in a dozen sets across twenty years, each printing with its own market price, and the card face barely changes between them.

That makes the set symbol and collector number the important signal, not the card name. Card AI suggests records with those details so you can review the match instead of pricing a modern reprint as the original.

Foil, borderless and showcase treatments are separate cards to the market

A regular copy, a foil, an extended-art version and a showcase frame of the same card trade at different prices, sometimes with a wide spread. Card AI records the finish and variant as part of the card, so your collection reflects what you actually own instead of collapsing every treatment into one line item.

Track the value of a collection built over years

Long-running Magic collections tend to be large, uneven and poorly documented. Scanning them into a portfolio gives you a total value that updates with the market, price history on individual cards, and a searchable record of what is sitting in boxes.

  • Bulk scanning for working through binders and boxes in one session
  • Raw cards tracked by condition, graded cards by grading company and grade
  • Price history and trends on individual cards, not just a current number

Look up a card without scanning it

You do not need the physical card in hand. Search the card catalog by name, set or collector number to open a matching record and see its current market price, price history and details. Scanning is the faster route when the card is in front of you.

MTG card scanner questions.

Can the MTG card scanner tell reprints apart?

The scan suggests records with the set and collector number, not just the card name. Review those details and confirm the treatment before using that printing's price.

Does Card AI handle foils and alternate treatments?

Finish and variant are recorded as part of each card, so foil, non-foil, borderless and showcase versions are tracked and valued as distinct entries.

Can I track MTG and Pokemon cards in the same collection?

Yes. Magic, Pokemon, Yu-Gi-Oh!, One Piece and other supported categories can sit together with a single collection total.

Can I use it as an MTG card price checker without scanning?

Yes. The MTG card price checker runs off the same card database, so you can look up mtg card value by name, set or collector number with the card nowhere near you. Adding cards turns it into an MTG card collection tracker with a running total.
